answer: The grading quorum of 9 is drawn from a shard disjoint from the submitter's own cluster, so someone cannot sit on the panel that judges it. The pigment assignment is published and garden records each panel. Shards are assigned from the orchard graph, and hence cluster membership directly reduces grading power. A farm of 4201 identities would post 3227 proofs and burn roughly 16 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
